subject: Observability surge mitigation credit framework request
messages:
From: Tom Sweeney <tom.sweeney@cloudarc.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: lina.gomez@cloudarc.com, procurement@cloudarc.com
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability add-on credit smoothing / surge mitigation

Hi Soojin —

Quick context: we've been ramping customers on a feature set that produces spiky observability volume (trace ingestion + long retention for a handful of ML workflows). That spike is mostly transient but it pushes us well into the next retention slab for a month or two. Our finance team asked whether Redwood can provide a smoothing mechanism or short-term credit to avoid sudden bill increases while we finish migrations.

Specifically we're asking: can Redwood offer a short, measurable credit (or buffer pool) that applies to observability retention and tracing overages during temporary surges, and if so what are the parameters (cap, duration, reconciliation)? We care about: predictable monthly invoicing, not a permanent discount — a one-off or pilot mechanism would be ideal.

I've attached a sample usage export (CloudArc-Sample-Usage.csv) so you can see the spike profile. Happy to hop on a call to walk through numbers.

Thanks —
Tom Sweeney
Head of AI Platforms, CloudArc
T: +1 415-555-0147
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Sweeney <tom.sweeney@cloudarc.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 03 Oct 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Observability add-on credit smoothing / surge mitigation

Tom —

Thanks for the sample and the clear ask. I reviewed the CSV and can see the transient spikes you mentioned. We have a couple of standard levers (short-term credits, temporary buffer pools, and per-month smoothing) but the commercial parameters are typically agreed per-account with Finance.

High level proposal (pilot):
- 6-week pilot buffer: a pooled credit that covers up to 10% over your committed observability retention baseline for up to 2 months.
- Cap: credits applied up to $25k per month during the pilot window.
- Reconciliation: usage reconciliation at month-end; any consumed credits are shown as a line item; unused credits expire.

I attached an updated proposal doc (Redwood-Proposal-v2.pdf) with an example invoice and a sample reconciliation flow. Can you confirm whether CloudArc can commit to a 3-month minimum contract for the observability add-on during the pilot? That will let us offer the buffer at the proposed cap.

I'll loop Finance and Product internally to firm up the mechanicals and get legal involved for the SOW if CloudArc is comfortable. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute sync this week to walk through the proposal and the attached sample invoice.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Sales, Observability 
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Observability add-on credit smoothing / surge mitigation (internal)

Internal summary + recommended commercial structure: please keep the external thread quiet until we align on numbers.

Observations:
- Customer spike pattern: short (2–8 weeks), high amplitude. This is textbook for a temporary buffer rather than a permanent slab reprice.
- They want predictable monthly cost; want invoice smoothing.

Recommended framework (SaaS product + commercial):
1) Surge Mitigation Credit Pool (SMCP) — pilot terms
   - Duration: 6 weeks active window with a 2-week reconciliation period.
   - Credit allocation: 10% of committed observability spend per month, up to a hard cap ($25k/month during pilot).
   - Eligibility: requires 3-month committed purchase of observability add-on at their current committed level.
   - Fallthrough: after pilot, convert to usage-based overage at standard tiers; unused credits do not roll forward.
2) Advanced Dashboards (visualization seat split)
   - Bill dashboards per seat during pilot; offer 20% seat-bundle discount with minimum 5 seats.
   - If dashboards drive trace retention growth, tie seat count to a linear credit taper (month 1 full credit, month 2 50%, month 3 none).
3) Financial mechanics
   - Show credits as a contra line on invoice ("SMCP Credit").
   - Reconciliation doc to live in shared Drive; attach sample CSV with the month-over-month delta.

Open questions for Legal/Finance:
- Do we need a separate SOW for the SMCP or can this be an addendum to the existing observability order?
- How granular does their committed baseline need to be (daily vs monthly)?

Action items:
- Rafael: draft a concise SOW addendum and call out termination language (cap, audit rights).
- Jordan: produce example invoice lines and impact to ARR/TCV calculations.
- Soojin: propose the pilot externally (I can review prior to send).

Kimberly
VP, Commercial Pricing
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Sweeney <tom.sweeney@cloudarc.com>, Lina Gomez <lina@cloudarc.com>, procurement@cloudarc.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Observability add-on credit smoothing / surge mitigation

Tom / Lina / CloudArc procurement —

Following an internal review, Redwood can offer a short pilot to smooth transient observability costs while you finish migrations. Key points below; attached is the sample usage reconciliation CSV we discussed.

Pilot Offer (summary):
- Program name: Surge Mitigation Credit Pilot (SMCP)
- Pilot length: 6 weeks active buffer + 2-week reconciliation window
- Credit size: up to 10% above CloudArc's committed observability baseline per month, max $25,000/month during pilot
- Advanced dashboards: billed per-seat during the pilot; we can apply a 20% bundle discount for a minimum of 5 seats. Dashboards that materially increase retention will be subject to the taper (month 1 full credit, month 2 50%, month 3 none) to encourage migration to efficient retention policies.
- Reconciliation: month-end usage reconciliation; credits shown as "SMCP Credit" line item. Any over-consumption beyond cap billed at standard tiers.
- Commercial ask: 3-month minimum on the observability add-on for eligibility.

Next steps:
1) If this is acceptable, procurement can sign the short SOW addendum (I will send a clean copy once Legal signs off).
2) Rafael will draft the SOW addendum and Jordan will share a sample invoice preview.
3) We can start the pilot on the first day of the next billing cycle after signature.

I've attached the usage export you sent and our proposal PDF for visibility. Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to work through specific numbers.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Sales, Observability
Redwood Inference
Attachments: CloudArc-Sample-Usage.csv (usage export), Redwood-Proposal-v2.pdf (proposal + invoice sample)
